sources.value: Original demonstration content: turn a learning goal into a small cycle of explanation, recall, feedback and scheduled practice.

blocks.label: The idea
blocks.text: Choose one thing you want to understand. Read a short explanation, close the source, and explain the idea in your own words. Use feedback to decide what to practise next.

blocks.label: A small, repeatable routine
items: Pick a narrow goal: explain a concept or complete a task.
Try to recall or apply it before looking at the answer.
Check your explanation and correct one specific gap.
Return to the difficult part in a later session.

blocks.label: The cycle
blocks.text:
CHOOSE A GOAL
  -> READ OR WATCH
  -> EXPLAIN FROM MEMORY
  -> CHECK AND CORRECT
  -> PLAN THE NEXT PRACTICE

blocks.label: An illustrative example
blocks.text: Goal: explain how a filter changes a list. Read one example, sketch the input and output from memory, then test a new input. The result gives you a concrete explanation to check.

blocks.label: Common mistake
blocks.text: A familiar-looking page can feel like understanding. Add a small task that reveals whether you can use the idea without looking.

blocks.label: Your turn
blocks.text: Name a topic you are learning. Write one sentence describing what you should be able to explain or do at the end of a short session.

blocks.label: The idea
blocks.text: Make an attempt to retrieve the idea before checking the source. The attempt gives you something specific to compare with a reliable explanation.

blocks.label: Useful prompts
items: Explain the concept to a beginner in three sentences.
Draw the process and label each step.
Predict the result of a small change.
Give an example and a counterexample.

blocks.label: Worked example
blocks.text: After reading about SQL joins, close the notes. Sketch two tiny tables and predict an inner join result. Then check the output and explain any difference.

blocks.label: Common mistake
blocks.text: Turning the task into copying. Put the source aside for the first attempt, then use it deliberately for feedback.

blocks.label: Try it now
blocks.text: Close this page and explain the learning cycle. Reopen it, identify one missing step, and improve your explanation. You do not need to reproduce the wording exactly.

blocks.label: The idea
blocks.text: A useful question tests a clear piece of understanding. Make it small enough to answer, and keep a way to check whether the answer is complete.

blocks.label: Build the question
items: Choose a concept or action, rather than an entire chapter.
Ask for explanation, prediction or a concrete example.
Keep the expected answer separate from the question.
Revise questions that are ambiguous or test only wording.

blocks.label: Question card
blocks.text:
FRONT
What changes when a list is filtered?

BACK
The displayed items follow a condition.
Explain the input, condition and resulting items.
Give a tiny example and check it.

blocks.label: A nested subtopic gets its own page
blocks.text: This page sits under Active recall in the topic inventory. Dedicated-page mode includes every hierarchy level, even when a subtopic has children of its own.

blocks.label: Make one card
blocks.text: Write a question for your current topic. Answer it without notes, then compare with the source. If you cannot decide whether the answer is right, improve the question or its checking guide.

blocks.label: The idea
blocks.text: Compare your attempt with a trustworthy source or a clear expected result. Look for a specific difference that you can correct and practise.

blocks.label: What to inspect
items: Was the main idea correct?
Did the explanation omit a condition or exception?
Does your example actually demonstrate the rule?
Can you explain the correction without copying the source?

blocks.label: Worked example
blocks.text: Your sketch says all source items appear in the filtered list. A small test shows only matching items. Correct the explanation, then try another condition to see whether you understand the change.

blocks.label: Common mistake
blocks.text: Reading the correct answer and moving on immediately. Try the corrected explanation once more, using a different example if possible.

blocks.label: Correction log
blocks.text:
My original answer: ____
The specific gap: ____
My corrected explanation: ____
A new example to check it: ____

blocks.label: The idea
blocks.text: Use what you noticed in practice to choose the next small task. A useful plan says what to practise and how you will check it, rather than only naming a chapter to reread.

blocks.label: Choose your next step
items: Keep one difficult question for another attempt.
Revisit the topic in a later session.
Change the example to check transfer.
Adjust the plan to your deadline and current understanding.

blocks.label: Keep the plan realistic
blocks.text: There is no universal schedule in this demonstration. Choose a manageable return time, then adjust according to your recall and the time available.

blocks.label: Before you finish
blocks.text: Write one task for the next session. Include the material you will need and one clear sign that the task is complete.
